newsitem.title: USA: Clinton talks to Kohl about future of NATO.
newsitem.headline: Clinton talks to Kohl about future of NATO.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl talked by telephone on Friday about European security issues and the future of NATO, the White House said.

Spokesman Mike McCurry said the conversation was part of a regular pattern of consultations Clinton will have with other European leaders in the months ahead of a Madrid summit in July of NATO leaders to announce the first new countries to join NATO.
The group is widely expected to include Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
McCurry was noncommittal on a French proposal for a big-power summit with Russia to clear the way for NATO expansion.

Diplomats in Paris said that under the proposal, leaders of the United States, Russia, France, Germany and Britain would meet in April to establish the broad lines of a deal that could enable Moscow to accept the enlargement of NATO.
McCurry said Clinton and visiting Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin discussed the concept.

"But I will restate our view that it is very important for individual members of NATO and leaders within NATO to continue the pattern of bilateral consultation that you've seen under way," he told reporters.
